content.text: I've reviewed every liability location. No monetary cap exists anywhere in the agreement; the structure is a symmetric standard-of-care exculpation plus an uncapped Servicer/Marketing Agent indemnity running to our side.

input.quote: Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable under this Agreement only for its specific obligations under this Agreement. All other liability is expressly waived and released as a condition of, and consideration for, the execution of this Agreement by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The liability architecture sits at or above the fallback on its material terms and is not adverse to us. (1) Mutuality: Section 6.2(a) (p0283) limits Cellco as Servicer/Marketing Agent to its specific obligations and to its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, and Section 5.2(a) (p0243) applies word-for-word the same limitation to the Depositor — the exculpation is symmetric in structure. (2) No monetary cap: there is no aggregate liability cap, no fee-based ceiling and no "shall not exceed" formula anywhere in the document (Section 9.7 is only a trustee capacity carve-out; Section 9.6 is limited recourse). The absence of a cap means the counterparty's exposure — including its Section 6.3 indemnities (p0291–p0292) for willful misconduct, bad faith and gross negligence in favour of the Issuer and the trustees — is uncapped, so the fallback carve-outs for indemnification, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are satisfied a fortiori. Inserting a mutual 12-months-of-fees cap would newly cap Cellco's uncapped indemnity and exculpate it above a Servicing Fee-based ceiling; that would weaken our position, so we do not redline it. (3) Our own exposure is additionally protected, not exposed: Section 9.6 (p0378) confines any claim against the Depositor or the Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property only — a one-sided de facto limit in our favour, with no equivalent limit for Cellco. Walk-away triggers are absent: our liability is not uncapped while Cellco's is capped, there is no sub-6-month cap, and indemnities are not inside any cap. Noted short of preferred, but not flagged: there is no free-standing mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (the bar on punitive and consequential damages at p0469 binds only the arbitral panel in dispute resolution proceedings), no USD 1,000,000 floor, no express confidentiality/data-protection or IP-infringement super-carve-outs, and no statement that payment obligations are outside the cap. Each of these is a preferred-only refinement that has no adverse effect while no cap exists.
